evals.prompt: Rate the UI of our dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:3000/ and tell me what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: Runs rankings.cjs all on every view of the dashboard plus Lighthouse, scores the expert rankings, and names the worst ranking with its findings and a first fix.
expectations: Runs scripts/rankings.cjs all with every reachable view as its own URL
Runs Lighthouse (mobile at least) or says why it could not
Reports each ranking as a number, not only prose
Names the lowest ranking first and one concrete fix for it

evals.prompt: Iterate on the settings page until every ranking is green, one ranking per round, and commit each round.
evals.expected_output: Measures a baseline, fixes one ranking per round worst first, re-runs that ranking and rankings.cjs all after each fix, and commits with before and after in the message.
expectations: Records a baseline for every ranking before changing code
Each round fixes one ranking and re-runs rankings.cjs all, not only the ranking it fixed
Each commit message names the ranking and its before and after numbers
Stops only when the measured rankings meet the --min target and states any ranking not run

evals.prompt: Make this page look cool and modern and rate it like the top design award sites would, until it's 8/10.
evals.expected_output: Takes shots in both themes at phone and desktop, rates with the ten-judge design panel and its anchors, changes the look in rounds while keeping every measured ranking, and reports the panel as one agent's judgment.
expectations: Uses rankings.cjs shots and rates from phone and desktop screenshots in light and dark
Scores all ten judges in references/design-panel.md and reports the mean
Re-runs rankings.cjs all after each look change and fixes any measured ranking that dropped
Says the rating is one agent's judgment against public criteria, not a jury
Rates with fresh blind rater subagents, never with its own scores
When blind scores stall below the target, stops and reports the gap and the options instead of claiming the target

evals.prompt: Just run Lighthouse on my homepage and give me the scores.
evals.expected_output: Points to web-quality-audit (or runs a single Lighthouse pass) rather than the full multi-round rankings workflow.
expectations: Does not start the multi-round rankings workflow for a single Lighthouse request
Mentions web-quality-audit or runs one Lighthouse pass and reports its category scores
Does not run the design panel or blind raters for a Lighthouse-only request

evals.prompt: The design panel sat near 7 for 17 rounds on placeholder art. I swapped in a realistic, model-drawn 12-page fixture, and the blind raters now give 6.7 and 6.2 instead of 7.2 and 6.8. Did the redesign get worse? What next?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the realistic fixture raised Content and Creativity but let raters see layout flaws the placeholder hid, so each capped every judge at 7. Treats the drop as a finding list, not a regression of the page, re-baselines on the new fixture, and fixes the flaws that two or more raters named before the next round.
expectations: Says the drop comes from the new fixture exposing layout flaws, not from a worse page
Lists the named flaws (for example a phone spread at half width, cut-off captions) as the next round's work
Re-baselines on the new fixture and does not compare new scores with the placeholder rounds
Does not go back to the placeholder fixture to win back the higher score

evals.prompt: Build a settings page for our web app with a list of 300 saved filters, light and dark mode, that works on phones.
evals.expected_output: Before writing UI the agent reads references/comfort-patterns.md and builds to it: 44 px targets, 14 px minimum text, the list capped with 'Show N more', state-specific controls with rare actions behind a menu, an accent checked for 4.5:1 contrast in both themes. It pins the comfort budget as gate tests (an axe + target + text + overflow audit over every view in both themes with reduced motion, and a tap-count test per everyday job), runs them, and reports the numbers.
expectations: Reads references/comfort-patterns.md before writing UI
Adds an audit test over every view on phone and desktop, light and dark, with reduced motion
Adds a tap-count test with a budget per everyday job
Caps the 300-item list instead of rendering all of it
Reports measured numbers, not an opinion

evals.prompt: I redesigned the app. Is the new design actually better than the old one?
evals.expected_output: The agent takes before and after screenshots of the same views, gives a fresh agent A/B pairs in random order, keeps the key in a folder that agent does not read, scores the verdicts against the key, and reports 'preferred on N of M screens' with the judge's reasons, then lists the real issues the judge named. It never answers from its own opinion of its work.
expectations: Before/after screenshots of the same views
A/B order randomized; the judge never sees the key
Reports preference as N of M screens, scored against the key
Lists the issues the judge named and which are real

evals.prompt: The comfort budget test passes on every view (no axe problems, no text under 14 px, no small targets, no sideways scroll), but the blind judge preferred the old design on the Week and Review screens. What now?
evals.expected_output: The agent opens the after screenshots of those two screens itself and names the cause (for example an id that spills over a narrow column, or a number that wraps over two lines after the text grew). It adds a spill check to the budget test (inline text wider than its block, number cells on more than one line), runs it on the crowded state the full suite builds, reverts the fix once to see the check fail, then fixes the CSS and re-runs the budget and the judge.
expectations: Reads the losing screens and names a concrete cause
Adds a check that fails on that cause (spill or broken number)
Runs the budget on the crowded state, not a fresh seed
Plants the regression once to prove the check fails, then fixes it

evals.prompt: The comfort budget passes and I redrew the approved pictures after the restyle. A reviewer read some of them. Can I say every block was checked visually?
evals.expected_output: No. The agent has a fresh agent read every approved picture, not a sample, and reports 'read N of M'. It fixes each real problem (an ISO date, a missing space, a doubled line), turns any it can into a check (a raw-ISO-date count in the budget), redraws only what changed, rereads the changed pictures itself, and runs the whole-set review once more on the final set before claiming it.
expectations: Requires every picture read, with a read-N-of-M count
Fixes real findings and adds a check where a machine can see them
Rereads changed pictures and repeats the whole-set review on the final set
Does not claim full coverage from a sample

evals.prompt: Redesign web/ with the design skill the owner chose. The current accent is indigo; nothing in the repo names a main color, and the owner's rules say to use their chosen main color.
evals.expected_output: Before it changes the accent, the agent searches config, design docs, and the owner's rules for a recorded main color. Finding none, it may change the hue, but the PR names the change with the old and new token values and one before/after pair, and says it is one token to change back.
expectations: Searches for a recorded main color before changing the accent
Names the hue change in the PR with old and new token values
Shows one before/after pair for the accent change
Says the accent is one token to change back

evals.prompt: Build a private one-page report for a machine setup goal. It has status, evidence, blockers and next actions, and must stay local.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained local report with readable text, measured contrast, phone and desktop layouts, and no published personal paths or data.
expectations: Keeps private machine data local
Uses at least 14 px text and 44 px interactive targets
Uses a responsive layout without horizontal scrolling
Distinguishes pending actions from verified success
Does not claim an accessibility score without running the audit

evals.prompt: A dashboard gate clicks a chart on a phone, presses ArrowLeft without reading the result, and has only an October fixture. Its exported hourly keys are local time and its chart-line contrast is untested. Harden the gate without claiming a stub host proves the real deployed dashboard.
evals.expected_output: Tests UTC identity through both clock changes, real touch selection and changed keyboard tooltip text, and 3:1 chart-line contrast in both themes. Plants broken handlers and low contrast to prove the gate detects each regression; labels fixture evidence and obtains real-host visual proof separately.
expectations: Keeps all 168 consecutive hourly fixture instants through both spring-forward and fall-back in exported and rendered points; does not impose 168 on a local calendar week
Uses touchscreen.tap on the phone and asserts the selected point changes
Asserts ArrowLeft changes tooltip text and plants a disabled handler to prove the assertion
Measures chart lines against their panels at 3:1 or more in light and dark, with a planted low-contrast failure
Keeps the host accent hue and clearly distinguishes fixture checks from real-host visual evidence

evals.prompt: Build a local HTML report for an OpenCode tooling-readiness goal. Hosted model, MCP, browser and doctor checks pass, but the configured local default times out and a protected .gitconfig apply needs a person. Keep it private and readable on a phone.
evals.expected_output: A self-contained local report whose first view says the goal is partly met or blocked, names both unresolved items before the passing evidence, and offers only real next actions. It uses readable responsive text, measured contrast, reduced-motion-safe presentation, and no private absolute paths or credentials. Accessibility claims require an actual audit.
expectations: Opens on the failed readiness criterion and required human decisions rather than a success banner
Keeps private machine paths and credentials out of the report
Uses at least 14 px text, 44 px interactive targets, and no sideways phone scroll
Separates verified passes, failures, pending checks, and next actions
Runs an accessibility audit before claiming one or reports it as not run

evals.prompt: Get our checkout page to pass 10 principal UI judges at 8 or more.
evals.expected_output: Reads judge-learnings.md, shoots phone/desktop x light/dark, writes context.txt and decisions.txt, runs ten blind lens judges from judge.mjs prompt, scores them with judge.mjs score, fixes consensus issues worst first, re-judges with new judges, and adds a judge-learnings line.
expectations: Reads references/judge-learnings.md before the first round
Each judge gets only the judge.mjs prompt for its lens, never earlier scores or the target
Scores with scripts/judge.mjs score, not with free scores the judges invent
Fixes only issues that two or more judges name, unless a blocker it can see itself
Adds a dated line to references/judge-learnings.md after the run
Reports the target as met only when judge.mjs score exits 0 for that round

evals.prompt: Run the 10-lens principal judge panel on 40 screenshots.
evals.expected_output: Splits lenses across agents (5 or fewer each), tells each to write r/<lens>.txt right after each lens, time-boxes them, and arms a background watchdog on r/ with a cap; scores what exists on timeout.
expectations: Gives each judge agent 5 lenses or fewer
Asks for r/<lens>.txt right after each lens
Arms a capped background watchdog on r/ and scores what exists on timeout

evals.prompt: A judge agent returns 10 lens verdicts after reading 6 of the 40 screenshots.
evals.expected_output: Rejects those verdicts, moves the files aside, and reruns the agent with a brief that requires reading every screenshot first and reporting the count read.
expectations: Does not score verdicts from a subset of shots
Reruns with a read-all-first rule
Asks the judge to report how many shots it read

evals.prompt: Three judge rounds in a row fixed every shared note, and the panel mean moved 8.12, 8.27, 8.16. The user asks whether to run another round.
evals.expected_output: Calls the movement noise, recommends stopping the judge rounds, and files the remaining notes as one checklist task with a numeric goal instead of another round.
expectations: Does not call a 0.1-0.3 change a regression or a gain
Recommends stopping after three flat rounds
Turns the remaining notes into a task with a measurable target

evals.prompt: A layout pilot passed its new tests (content covers 70% of the width, one filled button, adjacent tiles differ), but the judge panel mean fell from 7.15 to 7.07 and Week dropped 0.40. The desktop layout hides two sections the phone shows. Should we ship it and keep polishing?
evals.expected_output: Does not ship. Names the desktop/phone content gap as the cause, says the judge-worded tests were gamed, honors the pre-registered pivot, and calls further polish noise within ±0.3.
expectations: Does not ship a layout that hides content on desktop that the phone shows
Says tests copied from judges' wording can pass while the user-visible state is wrong
Honors a pre-registered pivot instead of polishing more
Treats mean moves within ±0.3 over three rounds as noise and recommends stopping the rounds

evals.prompt: Design round 3: the storyboard's Scroll stills look full, but all three raters, shown a motion strip of Page view for the first time, say each page fills only its top 60%. The catalogue raters ask for a verdict on every card, yet 156 of 215 takes in the fixture are unjudged because the judge run failed. What do you do next?
evals.expected_output: Fixes the page layout (row packing / panel shape) because every rater named it, rates every view mode from now on, and treats the missing verdicts as a fixture problem: rerun or repair the judge before redesigning the cards.
expectations: Treats a flaw named by all three raters as the next fix
Rates every view mode (motion or stills of each), not only the default view
Names the unjudged fixture as the cause of the missing card verdicts
Does not redesign the cards before checking the fixture's pipeline ran

evals.prompt: Design round 22: last round all three catalogue raters asked to remove the 'No reason recorded' line, and you removed it. Now two of three raters ask to add it back, and one rater asks for heavier toolbar shadows while another asks for lighter ones. What do you do before the next round?
evals.expected_output: Keeps a decision ledger copied to every rater folder, declines the reversal and the opposite shadow asks and logs them, adds a fixture fact about missing reasons, sharpens the rater prompt so raters may not reverse a ledger decision without a named hard flaw, then builds only the remaining shared fixes and re-rates with new raters.
expectations: Does not re-add the removed line just because two raters now ask for it
Writes or updates a DECISIONS.md ledger and gives it to the next raters
Declines the opposite-direction shadow asks and logs them as declined
Adds the missing reasons as a fixture fact or changes the rater prompt, so the judges are fixed before the next round
Keeps raters blind to earlier scores

evals.prompt: Rate a storyboard editor and a review catalogue (work tools, not marketing pages) with the design panel; the owner says 'until it passes 8.0'. Plan the panel and the stop rule.
evals.expected_output: Swaps spectacle judges (The FWA, Godly, CSS Winner) for app judges (Apple Design Awards, Nielsen heuristics, Material/HIG fit), rates a best-in-class reference of the same page type first and sets the target at its blind mean minus 0.3, caps fixes at one per element class per round, runs a structural A/B round after three rounds that each gain under 0.15, and budgets about 10 rounds.
expectations: Does not use The FWA and Godly unchanged for a work-tool page
Rates a best-in-class reference page with the same blind raters before round 1
Sets the target from the reference mean, not a fixed 8.0, and tells the owner why
Plans a structural A/B round when CSS rounds go flat
States a round budget
